chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mundhir ibn Yazid, from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever fasts for the sake of God, Mighty and Majestic, for a day during intense heat and thirst strikes him, God assigns a thousand angels with him, wiping his face and giving him glad tidings. Until when he breaks the fast, God, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: How sweet is your fragrance and your spirit! My angels, bear witness that I have indeed forgiven him.'

key_terms.رِيحَكَ وَرَوْحَكَ: Your fragrance and your spirit — poetic divine address praising the spiritual beauty and purity emanating from the fasting person
key_terms.صَامَ: Fasted — from sawm, the act of ritual fasting by abstaining from food, drink, and other things from dawn to sunset
key_terms.ظَمَأ: Thirst — specifically physical thirst experienced during fasting, here understood as a mark of sincere devotion
key_terms.وَكَّلَ: Assigned/entrusted — God entrusting specific angels to accompany the fasting person as a sign of divine honor
key_terms.يَمْسَحُونَ: Wiping/caressing — the angels' act of gently wiping the face as a gesture of comfort and blessing
key_terms.يُبَشِّرُونَهُ: Giving glad tidings — the angels announcing to the fasting person the divine reward that awaits him

ai.seo_question: What reward does God give to a person who fasts during intense heat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the immense spiritual reward for fasting during extreme summer heat. When a believer endures the hardship of thirst while fasting, God appoints a thousand angels to comfort him, and upon breaking the fast, God personally proclaims the fasting person's forgiveness before His angels. This hadith was transmitted to early Shia communities to encourage steadfastness in worship during challenging physical circumstances, conveying that sincere devotion to God — even amid bodily hardship — draws divine mercy and forgiveness.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Munzar Bin Yazeed, from Yunus Bin Zibyan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who Fasts for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for a day during intense heat, so thirst hits him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allocates a thousand Angels with him, wiping his face, and giving him glad tidings until when he breaks the Fast, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says to him: “How aromatic is your fragrance and your spirit. My Angels! Bear witness that I<sup>azwj</sup> have Forgiven him’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mundhir ibn Yazid from Yunus ibn Zabayan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one, for the sake of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, fasts on a very hot day, causing him to experience a great deal of thirst, Allah assigns a thousand angels for his safety who wipe his face until he discontinues his fast.’
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, then says, ‘How fine is your fragrance and spirit! O My angels, bear witness that I have granted him forgiveness.’”
